la:adj:alumnus.html:
ălumnus, a, um, adj.
qs. contr. of alomenos, from alo
.
That is nourished, brought up; for the most part subst.
ălumnus, i, m., a nursling, a pupil, foster-son.
Lit. (most freq. in the poets.): desiderio alumnūm ( = alumnorum), Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 116 Rib.): erus atque alumnus tuus sum,: quid voveat dulci nutricula majus alumno?; : Tityon, terrae omniparentis alumnum,; so ; cf. with 421: legionum alumnus,i. e. brought up in the camp,; cf. : Vatinius sutrinae tabernae alumnus,: suum flevit alumnum,: alumni hominum peccatorum, * .—Of the inhabitants of a country (cf. altrix): Italia alumnum suum summo supplicio fixum videret,; of cattle: Faune, abeas parvis Aequus alumnis,; so .—
Trop.: ego itaque pacis, ut ita dicam, alumnus,: alumnus fortunae,a child of fortune,.—Hence, of pupils: Platonis alumnus,pupil, disciple,: alumnus disciplinae meae,.—
ălumna, ae, f., a foster-daughter, a pupil: nostra haec alumna,: Italia omnium terrarum alumna eadem et parens (i. e. quae ab aliis terris alitur),: aliquam filiam et alumnam praedicare,: trepidam hortatur alumnam,.—Of frogs: aquai dulcis alumnae, Poët. ap. .—Trop.: cana veritas Atticae philosophiae alumna, truth, the foster-child of Attic philosophy, Varr. ap. : jam bene constitutae civitatis quasi alumna quaedam, eloquentia, the foster-child of an already well-ordered state, * : cliens et alumna Urbis Ostia (as a colony of the same),.—
The neutr.: numen alumnum,.—
In late Lat., act., nourishing; or subst., nourisher, one who brings up or educates: cygnus alumna stagna petierat,.—Hence Isidorus: et qui alit et alitur, alumnus dici potest, Orig. 10, 1.

la:verb:alucinor.gloss: to wander in mind, talk idly, prate, dream
senses: to wander in mind, talk idly, prate, dream
la:verb:alucinor.html:
ālūcĭnor (better than all- or hall-; cf. Gron. ad ), ātus, 1, v. dep.
prob. from ἀλύω, ἀλύσσω; ἄλη, ἀλύκη; cf.
,
to wander in mind, to talk idly, prate, dream (syn.: aberro, deliro, desipio, insanio): alucinari: aberrare et non consistere, atque dissolvi et obstupefieri atque tardari, (apparently not used before the time of Cic., yet cf. alucinatio): quae Epicurus oscitans alucinatus est,: suspicor hunc alucinari,; : indicium vagi animi et alucinantis,: epistolae nostrae debent interdum alucinari,to follow no definite train of thought, to digress freely, : alucinans pastor,.

la:noun:alum.html:
alum (hal-), n., or alus, i, f.,
a plant.
Comfrey: Symphytum officinale, Linn.; ; ; .—
A kind of garlic, .

senses: That which is made of it
la:noun:aluta.html:
ălūta, ae, f., orig. adj. (sc. pellis) [prob. from alumen],
a kind of soft leather, prob. prepared by means of alum.
Lit.: alutae tenuiter confectae, * : nigra,.—Hence,
That which is made of it.
A shoe: nivea,: nigra,: rupta,.—
A purse or pouch: tumidā superbus

alutā, .—

A patch put on the face for ornament, .
